content_text: from this transcript, the thing that stayed w/ me most is how often Todd Combs frames everything in confidence intervals 1. "what are earnings in 5 years, at a 90% confidence interval" 2. "how many co's will compound at 7%, at a 50% confidence interval" 3. "where is this company in its lifecycle using xyz confidence interval" this is really the correct way to think about anything in markets, where everything is just a range of outcomes and probability weightings...nothing is certain, nothing is discrete this framework takes time to get used to, there was a tweet a while back from a random account with a transcript of Peter Thiel talking about some company, and the tweet had a lot of engagement along the lines of "why does he talk about investing like this?" it took me a little to see what they were talking about. blind spots like a motherfucker its definitely a public markets thing where you constantly appear uncertain, and hedge all your statements, but thats the way it goes, and its consonant with how assets are priced i'll go try and dig the tweet up now but I just wanted to highlight the confidence interval language, I feel like its not as common as it should be + is a term I'll prob lean on more in the future.
